first_fail_evidence: All three repeats at n=4250 raise RuntimeError CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES and summary.failure_kind_at_wall is memory_wall. n=4062 completes on all three repeats, so the limit is the last completed rung, not an SLO crossing.

shape_fit.fit_note: n < 3500 has a single passing rung (2000), so the two-parameter fit uses the passing rungs with n <= 3500

gpu_mem_note: Result files record peak_commit_bytes and peak_rss_bytes on completed repeats. Failed repeats record memory_at_failure (rss_mb, used_mb, available_mb) and no GPU-memory field.

f16_322b2f86.same_n_note: The f16 search rungs are 3000, 3156, 3312, 3625, 4250, 5500. The only n shared with 69234ed5 is 4250, and every f16 repeat at 4250 failed before a prefill was recorded.

Due to a driver bug, any subsequent OpenCL API call may cause the application to hang, so the GPU plugin may be unable to finish correctly. The CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES error typically occurs in two cases: 1. Insufficient memory for the current inference. 2. An out-of-bounds access to GPU memory from a kernel. For case 1 (Insufficient Memory) - Try adjusting some model parameters (e.g., using a smaller batch size, lower inference precision, fewer streams, etc.) to reduce the required memory size. - Alternatively, for Intel integrated Arc GPUs on Microsoft Windows 10 or 11 host systems with more than 10 GB of system memory, the shared memory allocation can be increased via the Intel Graphics Software tool: 'Graphics > General > Shared GPU Memory Override', as long as it is not already at its software-defined upper limit. For case 2 (Out-of-Bounds Access): - Please submit a bug report to the OpenVINO team. Additionally, please try updating the driver to the latest version.
